variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host.

job_id returned by POST /assess. Fill in after submitting to run GET /jobs/:jobId, GET /jobs/:jobId/progress, POST /jobs/:jobId/cancel, DELETE /jobs/:jobId, and every request in the Artifacts folder. `phase` values progress staging → pending → processing → completed | failed, or cancelled from any of the first three (POST /jobs/:jobId/cancel).

A file name in the job's artifact directory — see GET /jobs/:jobId/artifacts for the list. n is the job's global ITEM index (every page of every document; the manifest's `items` map says which document and page n is). Written at job time: `regions.json`, `manifest.json`, `p<n>.base.jpg` (per item with a page image), one `text.p<n>.<key>.json` per item and distinct text layer the criteria used (`text.p0.auto.json`, `text.p0.always.json`, `text.p1.never.json`, …), and `text.d<i>.<key>.json` for a scope-document text search. Rendered on FIRST FETCH and then cached: `p<n>.svg`, `p<n>.layer.png`, `p<n>.preview.jpg`, and per criterion `p<n>.<slug>.svg` / `.layer.png` / `.preview.jpg`. Always available as a view: `text.p<n>.<key>.txt` / `text.d<i>.<key>.txt` (the layer's text, plain).

Base64 of unit-tests/classifier/documents/invoice_native.pdf, WITHOUT a data: prefix, for the JSON-body items. Fill it once: `base64 -w0 unit-tests/classifier/documents/invoice_native.pdf` (macOS: `base64 -i … | tr -d '\n'`; PowerShell: [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('…'))) and paste the output into this variable's CURRENT VALUE.
reference_id returned by POST /references (`r` + 12 hex). Fill in to run the References folder's GET / PATCH / DELETE items and the /assess items that list a reference.
A reference file name: page.jpg, working.jpg, c.<slug>.jpg (GET /references/:referenceId lists them), regions.json or record.json.

formdata.description: A document: JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF, AVIF, PDF (every page is an item), SVG, .txt or .docx. REPEAT the part for more documents — this item sends two. The kind is detected from the bytes (common.documents.detect_kind), never from the filename or Content-Type. The `src` points at a repo fixture — re-select the file if your Postman working directory differs. The legacy part name `image` is also accepted, and repeats too.
A second document, as a repeated `file` part: one more item. Parts are taken in form order.
JSON array of criterion objects — the same shape the JSON body's `criteria` takes, sent ONCE: it covers every document. See GET /criterion-types.
Optional, once: the job's model — a registry id from GET /models (default: the registry's). A criterion's options.model wins over it. Unknown or unavailable is a 400.

request.description:
The same request as the multipart POST /assess, as a JSON body: `{"documents": [{"type": "base64", "data": "…", "filename": "…"}], "criteria": [...]}` — a one-item `documents` list. `filename` is optional and only recorded in `documents[i].filename`. Fill the `invoice_native_b64` collection variable first (see its description). Returns 202 with a job_id. Same errors as POST /assess, plus 400 for invalid base64, both `document` and `documents`, or a body that is not a JSON object. See API.md § Request.

#### Schemas

See *POST /assess*, the first request of this endpoint.

`type: "url"` — the service fetches the URL AT SUBMIT (the item cap needs the bytes: a PDF counts its pages), after the SSRF check (common.net: private, loopback and link-local addresses are refused). This item uses the one-document shorthand `{"document": {…}}`, which is a one-item `documents` list — sending both keys is a 400. Returns 202. **400** for a blocked or unresolvable URL, **502** when the fetch fails, plus every POST /assess 400. Replace the example URL with a real document.

#### Schemas

See *POST /assess*, the first request of this endpoint.

`type: "text"` — the document IS the string, treated as a .txt (UTF-8), one item. No page image, so `cv` / `detector` units are SKIPPED, `score: false` is refused (no document in the request has an image), and the llm prompt is text-only. `documents[0].filename` is `inline.txt`. Returns 202. Errors as POST /assess.

See *POST /assess*, the first request of this endpoint.

item.name: POST /assess — JSON, job model and a per-criterion options.model

request.description:
Model selection. `model` (top level) is the JOB's model — a registry id from GET /models — used by every llm criterion (and cv llm fallback) without its own `options.model`, and by the `references: "auto"` selection call; omitted, the registry default (muse-glimmer). A criterion's `options.model` wins over it: here "states a due date" runs on qwen2.5-vl (the vllm-qwen-vl service — it must be running, or that criterion comes back `status: "error"`). Each result's `detail.model` names the model that answered, and the result's `request.model` is the job model, resolved. 400 for an unknown or unavailable id (the message lists the valid ones), and for what an effective model cannot do: a text-only model (`vision: false`) with `options.boxes`, with `references`, as a cv llm fallback, as the job model with `references: "auto"`, or on a photo while OCR is off; any model with fewer than 2 images per prompt with `references`. Returns 202 with a job_id. See API.md § Models.

#### Schemas

See *POST /assess*, the first request of this endpoint.

item.name: POST /assess — JSON, fast and adaptive modes per criterion (a one-token readout, escalated when unsure)

request.description:
Fast and adaptive modes, per criterion. `options.mode: "fast"` answers an llm criterion with reasoning OFF and ONE generated token — the criterion's rubric on the digits 0-9 (score = digit + 1), read from that token's top alternatives and their probabilities instead of from what the model wrote. No JSON, no stated confidence, no model-written reason; ~0.16 s per readout measured on qwen3.8-solo on a small image, ~0.3-0.6 s expected on a real page, against seconds for a reasoned call. `mode` is `reasoned` (the default; null is the same), `fast` or `adaptive`, per criterion only — a request-level `mode` is a 400 (a request's `model` has a job default because job-wide calls need one; nothing job-wide has a mode). `fast` runs only on a model whose models.yaml entry has a `fast` block (GET /models `supports.fast`; GET /criterion-types `mode.fast_models`): qwen3.8-solo and qwen3.5-4b — not the default muse-glimmer, so each fast criterion here names `options.model`. Here: two fast criteria (they share the page's cached prompt prefix), one explicitly reasoned on the same model, a fast presence criterion with `boxes: true` — the box loop runs after the readout, reasoned, exactly as after a reasoned score — and two ADAPTIVE criteria. `options.mode: "adaptive"` runs the same readout on the criterion's model, then — when its confidence is under the threshold or it could not be read (incomplete, or the probability cap) — today's reasoned scoring call on the ESCALATION model (CLASSIFIER_ESCALATION_MODEL, default the registry default muse-glimmer; GET /models `escalation` shows it and its host, which may be external) answers instead, never guided by references. The threshold is `options.escalate_below` (0-100, adaptive only — 85 on the first), else the model's models.yaml `fast.escalate_below.rating` (GET /models `fast.escalate_below`; 80 unless the entry sets it — the second). An adaptive result that stood is the readout's (`detail.mode: "fast"`); an escalated one is the escalation model's (`detail.mode: "reasoned"`, `detail.model` the escalation id, its own `detail.confidence` and model-written reason). `detail.escalation` = `{escalated, model, threshold, signal, why, error, fast}` — `why` e.g. "confidence 62 < 80", `fast` the readout it replaced (only when it escalated). A failed escalation keeps a complete readout's answer (`escalated: false`, `error`); only an unreadable readout whose escalation failed errors the unit. Each escalation is one more llm_calls row, label `escalate/<name>`, kind `escalate`. Each fast result: `verdict` = the band (FAIL 1-3, MARGINAL 4-6, PASS 7-10) with the most probability, `score` = the most probable score inside it, `confidence` = round(100 × that band's probability), `reason` = "Fast readout (no reasoning): PASS 0.93, MARGINAL 0.05, FAIL 0.02.", `detail.mode: "fast"` and `detail.confidence` with `method` / `source` / `headline` `readout`, `stated: null` and `unseen_bound`. `detail.mode` / `options_used.mode` appear only when `options.mode` was sent. Errors (400, at submit): `mode` at the request's or a criterion's top level; `options.mode` on a text / detector / cv criterion; a value other than reasoned / fast / adaptive; `fast` or `adaptive` on a model with no `fast` block (naming the mode, where the model came from and the fast-capable ids); `options.reference` on a fast or adaptive criterion (references never guide a readout); `escalate_below` with a mode other than adaptive, outside 0-100, or on a text / detector / cv criterion; `adaptive` while the escalation model is unavailable (its API key unset — the message names CLASSIFIER_ESCALATION_MODEL); `adaptive` with a text-only escalation model on a photo with OCR off or options.ocr 'never'. At run time a readout is posted once, never retried; an incomplete one (coverage under fast.min_coverage), a capped one (the probability cap, fast.max_unseen_mass) or a server refusing top_logprobs fails that criterion alone with `status: "error"` and a message naming the fix ("— use mode 'reasoned' for this criterion"); in adaptive mode an incomplete or capped readout escalates instead. Deploy order: an older classifier refuses `mode` (and `escalate_below`) as an unknown key, so deploy the classifier first (GET /criterion-types → `mode` confirms the build; `mode.adaptive` the adaptive one). Returns 202 with a job_id. See API.md § Fast mode — a one-token readout and § Adaptive mode — escalate when unsure.

#### Schemas

See *POST /assess*, the first request of this endpoint.

formdata.value: NOTICE TO OWNER — Under Florida law, those who work on your property…
formdata.description: Inline text, treated as a .txt document (one item). Repeatable, and may be mixed with `file` parts — each is one document.
JSON array of criterion objects — the same shape the JSON body's `criteria` takes, sent ONCE: it covers every document. See GET /criterion-types.

request.description:
The multipart spelling of inline text: a `text` form field instead of (or alongside) a `file` part. Parsed into the same AssessRequest as the JSON `type: "text"` document, so the two produce identical results. Returns 202. **400** when there is no `file` / `text` at all, or a `text` field is empty.

#### Schemas

See *POST /assess*, the first request of this endpoint.

item.name: POST /assess — JSON, documents list (a PDF, a URL and inline text)

request.description:
Several documents in ONE job: `documents` is a list, each entry `{type: base64 | url | text, data, filename?}`, in order. Every page of every document is one item — here invoice_native.pdf (1 page) + the URL's document + the inline text = 3 items, when the URL is an image or a one-page PDF. Fill `invoice_native_b64` and replace the example URL first.

Each criterion runs once per item and is aggregated: `Notice to Owner` uses the text default (`sum`: hit counts added across items and documents, so ONE hit anywhere passes); `Notice to Owner in every document` keeps the `sum` pages rule but sets `documents: all` (= worst), so every document must have it; `has a signature` is PASS if any page of any document shows one; `sharpness` (cv: worst / worst) is skipped on the text item and excluded, so the worst of the two images decides. Each result entry's `items` lists the per-item answers, and the top-level `items` the per-item scores. Returns 202; same errors as POST /assess (a document is named `#<index> <filename>` in its error). See API.md § Documents, pages and items.

#### Schemas

See *POST /assess*, the first request of this endpoint.

item.name: POST /assess — multipart, repeated files and text fields

formdata.description: Document 0 — a two-page PDF: items 0 and 1.
Document 1 — a repeated `file` part: item 2.
Document 2 — inline text, a repeatable field: item 3.
JSON array of criterion objects — the same shape the JSON body's `criteria` takes, sent ONCE: it covers every document. See GET /criterion-types.

request.description:
Repeated multipart parts: two `file` parts and a `text` field are three documents and FOUR items (the PDF has two pages). The service takes them in form order — note that some clients (httpx `files=` / `data=`, requests) send every plain field before every file, which makes the inline text document 0; the result's `documents` / `items` say which is which.

`Net 30` (text, sum): found on the PDF's page 2 and in the text → PASS, `detail.count` 2, `detail.counts` per document. `Net 30 on every page` (`aggregate: "all"` at both levels) → FAIL: page 1 of the PDF and the photo do not have it. `has text` (`score: false`) returns block boxes on the PDF pages and the photo, each region with its item as `page`. Returns 202. See API.md § Documents, pages and items.

#### Schemas

See *POST /assess*, the first request of this endpoint.

Guide llm criteria with stored examples. Each llm-answered criterion finds its examples among the listed references' usable criteria by ONE matching order, the first that is set deciding: (1) `options.reference.criterion` → the reference criterion with that NAME; (2) the criterion's `key` → the reference criteria with that KEY, whatever either is named — a keyed criterion never falls back to its name; (3) otherwise its own `name`. Case-insensitive. Only (1) unmatched is a 400; an unmatched key or name scores unguided (`detail.reference.applied: false`, a note naming the key). Keys may repeat here — both `has a company logo` and `is there a brand mark` carry `logo`, so the reference's `logo` example guides both — but are unique within a reference; the key is never shown to the model (the caption quotes the reference criterion's name). `references.criteria[name].matched_by` (criterion | key | name) says which rule applied, and each `per_criterion_scores` entry echoes its `key`. API.md § How a criterion finds its examples — the matching order. With a PASS and a FAIL example the scoring call is ONE contrastive call with three images (example, counter-example, candidate). `options.reference`: use, criterion, position (off | check — needs boxes; a miss caps the score), min_iou, combine (any | all | mean), and for the box loop `boxes` ({ask, refine, verify} — which of its calls are shown the examples) and `text` (each example's caption quotes its region's text) — both need options.boxes: true, unset = the CLASSIFIER_REFERENCE_BOX_* service defaults. The answer is in each unit's `detail.reference` and the result's top-level `references`; the job writes references.json (its `calls`, one list with a `kind` each: `scoring`, or the box loop's `box_ask` / `box_refine` / `box_verify` when the criterion's options.reference.boxes (service default: the CLASSIFIER_REFERENCE_BOX_* knobs) shows the loop the examples — FAIL examples only when the reference criterion's hint is presence, region crops for the ask under position: check; API.md § What the model is shown). Errors: 400 for every reference rule (no references with options.reference, options.reference on text / detector / OpenCV cv, unknown ids, an options.reference.criterion no listed reference has, more than CLASSIFIER_REFERENCE_MAX_PER_CRITERION examples, position check vs a whole-page example, …); 409 a reference not ready. Set `referenceId` first. See API.md § References.

#### Schemas

See *POST /assess*, the first request of this endpoint.

item.name: POST /assess — JSON, criteria inherited from references

request.description:
`criteria` omitted with explicit reference ids → the references' own criteria, merged by name in list order (a name defined differently in two references — a differing `key` included — is a 400 naming both; inherited criteria keep their keys, so they match by key). The result's `request.criteria` shows what ran and `references.inherited` is true. Without references an omitted `criteria` still means the four default quality criteria.

#### Schemas

See *POST /assess*, the first request of this endpoint.

item.name: POST /assess — JSON, references auto with tags

request.description:
Let the service pick examples: the pool is fixed at submit (ready references with a usable criterion that one of these criteria matches by the same matching order — options.reference.criterion, else `key`, else `name`; a keyed criterion admits references by key only — carrying all / any of the tags, newest first, at most CLASSIFIER_REFERENCE_AUTO_POOL_MAX); each page item then makes ONE selection call (the page as its one image plus a text catalogue of the pool), and each criterion keeps the matches that have a criterion it matches, at or above CLASSIFIER_REFERENCE_AUTO_MIN_CONFIDENCE. A failed selection only degrades — the error is in `references.selection`. `criteria` is required (400 without).

#### Schemas

See *POST /assess*, the first request of this endpoint.

item.name: POST /assess — JSON, box-loop options per criterion (marks for a text field, examples for a picture)

request.description:
Turn the bounding-box loop's opt-in settings on PER CRITERION — This example turns every option on to show the syntax. The MEASURED setup (ZT-527, API.md § The LLM enforcement loop): a one-line text field such as an amount due with `refine: "marks"` + `reference.boxes` (all three); a chart such as a usage history with `reference.boxes` (all three, no marks) + a FAIL reference of each look-alike; `verify_partial`, `verify_min_span` and `reference.text` only for a field that is still hard to identify. each needs `options.boxes: true`, and each left unset takes this container's service default (the env var, off), so two criteria on one page run the loop two ways. On an llm criterion's options: `refine` (grid | marks — marks numbers the text lines in the refine window and the box is the union of the lines the model picks: exact on a text field like an amount due, wrong for a chart or a logo, so leave those on grid; the lines are a digital PDF's own (exact, no OCR), else the OCR lines of the criterion's text layer, else an OCR pass of the refine window (never under `ocr: "never"`) — the attempt's `marks_lines` says which; with no line in the window the grid refine runs instead, saying so in `marks_fallback`), `verify_partial` (bool — the verify also says whether the crop cut the feature off; a rejected cut-off crop is retried in the same place, larger; never moves the score), `verify_min_span` (0-1 — the verify crop grown to this share of the page, so a one-line field keeps its label). Under options.reference (with `references` on the request): `boxes` ({ask, refine, verify} — which loop calls are shown the criterion's examples; same calls, 1 + examples images each) and `text` (each example's caption quotes its region's text, OCR'd once per job). A FAIL reference of a look-alike (its reference criterion's hint presence) is shown after the PASS one as 'the outlined thing is NOT …; do not box it'. Each result's `options_used` shows the values that RAN; `localization.attempts` records `refine_mode` / `marks` / `verify_partial`, and `localization.references` which steps carried examples. The loop never changes a score or a verdict. Errors (400): any of these without `boxes: true` (every one sent is named), `verify_min_span` outside 0-1, `refine` other than grid / marks, options.reference without `references`, `reference.boxes` / `reference.text` on a cv criterion, the llm keys on text / detector / cv (unknown keys). Deploy order: an older classifier refuses these keys, so deploy the classifier before a caller sends them (GET /criterion-types → `box_loop` confirms the build). Set `referenceId` first; a criterion its reference does not have scores unguided, with a note. Returns 202 with a job_id. See API.md § The box loop's options — per criterion and § Turning the box-loop options on for a document.

#### Schemas

See *POST /assess*, the first request of this endpoint.

query.description: staging | pending | processing | completed | failed | cancelled

request.description:
List jobs, newest first (common.jobs.router). Query `phase` filters by phase, `limit` (default 50) caps the page. Each row is `{job_id, phase, created_at, updated_at, elapsed_seconds, metadata: {type, request_id}, result, error}` — `metadata.type` is always `assess` (rows queued by an older container may say `compare` / `locate`; those fail with a message naming the removed type). Results can be large — prefer GET /jobs/:jobId.

#### Schemas

Response `200` (`application/json`):

```json
{"$ref": "#/$defs/classifier_jobs"}
```

Uses: `classifier_jobs`, `jobs_list_response`, `classifier_job`, `JobBase`, `job_base`, `job_id`, `job_metadata`, `assess_result`, `reference_result`, `reference_id`, `progress`, `document_entry`, `item_row`, `breakdown`, `criterion_entry`, `job_artifacts`, `references_summary`, `criterion_input`, `job_usage_block`, `progress_stage`, `ocr_layer`, `document_layer`, `region`, `criterion_artifacts`, `localization`, `unit_entry`, `llm_detail`, `text_detail`, `detector_detail`, `cv_detail`, `file_label`, `layer_links`, `usage_totals_fields`, `text_link`, `box_attempt`, `detail_llm_mean`, `detail_llm`, `aggregate_block`, `detail_text_mean`, `detail_text`, `detail_detector_mean`, `detail_detector`, `detail_cv_mean`, `detail_cv`, `cv_measurements`, `measurements_check_blur`, `measurements_check_exposure`, `measurements_detect_faces`, `measurements_detect_sky`, `measurements_detect_text`, `measurements_detect_vegetation`, `measurements_detect_water` — too large to show inlined (over 64 KiB), so its `$ref`s are kept; each definition is shown once under *Schema definitions* at the end of the collection's description.

query.description: Long-poll: seconds to hold the request until the job's phase is completed, failed or cancelled (default 0 — answer at once). A finite number >= 0; above 60 it is clamped to 60 (JOB_WAIT_MAX_S, under Cloudflare's ~100 s on api.zeoenergy.com); -1 / nan / inf are a 422. Pollers send min(30, time left).

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess (202 body). Paste it here, or set the collection variable `jobId`.

request.description:
Poll one job — once, or long-polled with `?wait=<seconds>` (enable the `wait` query param): the service re-reads the job every 0.5 s and answers the moment its phase is completed, failed or cancelled, or when the wait (clamped to 60 s) runs out, with the same body and the same 200 either way — read `phase`. Through this pass-through every poll is one metered LiteLLM request, so a poller sends `wait=min(30, time left)` (one or two requests per job instead of ~20) and, when a non-terminal answer came back in under a second (an older classifier ignores `wait`), sleeps its old interval before asking again. **422** for a negative, nan or inf `wait`; **404** for an unknown job, or one deleted mid-wait. See API.md § `GET /jobs/{job_id}`.

`phase` progresses staging → pending → processing → completed | failed, or turns cancelled from any of the first three (POST /jobs/:jobId/cancel — no `result`, no `error`). While it runs, `metadata.progress` says how far along it is: `{state, percent, stage, stage_title, label, index, length, attempt, seq, updated_at, stages}` — `state` queued → running → done | failed | cancelled, `percent` 0-100 (100 only once done; done / failed are written before the phase turns completed / failed, cancelled after the phase turned cancelled, once the runner has stopped), flushed about once a second (CLASSIFIER_PROGRESS_FLUSH_INTERVAL_S). Stages: assess = load (10) → units (85) → artifacts (5); reference = load (5) → units (70) → artifacts (5) → finalize (20). The checkpoint history is GET /jobs/:jobId/progress. See API.md § Progress.

When `completed`, `result` is the assessment:

Result shape (GET /jobs/:jobId → `result`, `schema_version: 3`):
  `{schema_version, documents, items, assessment: {overall_score, overall_verdict, complete, weighted_score_breakdown, per_criterion_scores}, verdict, page_geometry, detector, artifacts, references, request, usage}`
Every page of every document is one ITEM, numbered globally in request order. `documents[]` is `{index, filename, kind, pages, items, document_info}` (document_info: content_type, size_bytes, has_image, native_text_chars, ocr.layers per item, ocr.document_layers, llm_text_char_budget). `items[]` is `{item, document, page, filename, overall_score, overall_verdict, complete}` — each item's own weighted score. `page_geometry` is a list, one entry per item (null sizes for a .txt/.docx item); `page` there, a region's `page` and the `p{n}` layer prefix all mean the item.
Every entry of `per_criterion_scores` has the SAME keys — the AGGREGATED answer: `status` (ok | error | skipped), `type`, `key` (the criterion's reference-matching key, null when unset), `method`, `scored`, `score`, `verdict`, `confidence`, `reason`, `detail`, `regions` (the union over every item, capped at CLASSIFIER_INLINE_REGIONS_MAX with `regions_truncated`), `artifacts` (`items`: per item, that page's layer URLs filtered to the criterion and its loop `attempts`; `text`: one link per text layer its units read), `localization` (llm: the loop's record — merged across items; an attempt adds `refine_mode` (marks | grid), `marks`, `marks_shown`, `marks_lines` (native | ocr | window — which lines the marks call numbered: the PDF's own, the OCR layer's, or an OCR pass of the window), `marks_fallback` only with `refine: "marks"` (options.refine; service default CLASSIFIER_LLM_BBOX_REFINE_MODE) and `verify_partial` only with `options.verify_partial` (service default CLASSIFIER_LLM_BBOX_VERIFY_PARTIAL) (API.md § The LLM enforcement loop); with references, `localization.references` lists what the loop was shown, one entry per unit: `{item, applied, ask_images: composite | crop | null, examples (each with `text` under options.reference.text, service default CLASSIFIER_REFERENCE_BOX_TEXT), ask, refine, verify, note}` — `applied: false` with a note when every step is off (the criterion's options.reference.boxes; service default the CLASSIFIER_REFERENCE_BOX_* knobs) or no example has a region; absent without references), `options_used` (with `aggregate` resolved — and an llm criterion's box-loop settings `refine`, `verify_partial`, `verify_min_span`, plus `reference.boxes` / `reference.text` when `reference` was sent, as they RAN: the criterion's value, else this container's service default; API.md § The box loop's options — per criterion), `error`, `complete` (false when any of its units errored), `aggregate_used` ({pages, documents}), and `items` — one entry per unit: `{item, document, page, status, score, verdict, confidence, reason, detail, error, regions (a COUNT), text_layer, localization (llm)}`.
The overall score and verdict are weighed over the AGGREGATED criterion results; `complete` is false when any scored criterion is incomplete, and `overall_score` / `overall_verdict` are then null with the partial score in `weighted_score_breakdown` (`partial: true`). `score: false`, skipped and errored criteria never count toward the score. An `llm` entry's (and item's) `confidence` is the model's STATED 0-100 unless its models.yaml entry says `headline: calibrated` with a fitted calibration; `detail.confidence` carries the MEASURED confidence, per the entry's `confidence.method` (logprobs | sampling | stated): `{method, source (logprobs | sampling | stated — the fallback, with `note` saying why), headline (stated | calibrated), stated, stated_defaulted, calibrated, verdict_probability (mass on the reported verdict's band, a lower bound), band {PASS, MARGINAL, FAIL}, distribution {"1".."10"}, expected_score, entropy_bits, certainty, coverage, unresolved [{values, mass}], samples (sampling: {asked, answered, agreement, stated_mean}), note}` — null for a `score: false` criterion, only in `items[]` under `mean`. A guided call row in `detail.reference.calls[]` adds `verdict_probability`. One file per ITEM and distinct text layer, named `text.p<n>.<key>.json` — the key is the settings: `auto`, `always`, `never` (a future non-default OCR setting adds a hash: `auto-1a2b3c4d`) — and shared by every criterion that used those settings on that page. Each unit's entry links its own (`items[].text_layer = {key, url, source, chars}`), the criterion lists them all (`artifacts.text = [{item, key, url, source, chars}, …]`), and `options_used.ocr` agrees with the key.

Body: `{key, item, settings: {mode, min_native_chars, engine}, source: native|ocr|none, engine: "rapidocr"|null, chars, confidence, text, lines: [{text, polygon, confidence}]}`. `text` is byte-for-byte the string `match_text` searched, so a failed match can be diagnosed from this file alone. `lines` are the OCR lines with polygons in ORIGINAL page pixels; empty for native text (.txt, .docx, and native PDF text, whose line geometry is not recorded).

A text criterion with `options.scope: "document"` searched `text.d<i>.<key>.json` instead: `{key, scope: "document", document, settings, separator: " ", source, chars, text, segments: [{item, page, start, end, page_offset, file}]}` — the document's pages' layers joined in page order, and where each page sits in the joined string.

Set `artifactName` to `text.p0.auto.txt` for the same text as `text/plain; charset=utf-8`. Written for every job whose criteria read text, native or OCR'd; never dropped by the byte cap; deleted with the job. **404** when the job has no layer by that name.

#### Schemas

See *Artifacts / GET /jobs/:jobId/artifacts/:artifactName*, the first request of this endpoint.

item.name: Usage
item.description: What each job's vision-model requests cost. Every HTTP request to a model (a models.yaml entry) is one row of the `llm_calls` table in the classifier-db Postgres (also readable from Trino as postgres_classifier.public.llm_calls), linked to its job, criterion and item; the rows outlive the job's TTL and go only with DELETE /jobs/:jobId. A completed job's result carries the totals as `usage`. Set `jobId` from a POST /assess or POST /references response. See API.md § Model usage.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess (202 body). Paste it here, or set the collection variable `jobId`. An expired job's id still works here — the usage rows outlive the job.

request.description:
Every vision-model HTTP request the job made — each scoring call, box-loop ask / refine / verify, `references: "auto"` selection, reference description, and each parse retry, failed requests included — with its totals. Returns `{job_id, job_present, job_type, totals, by_kind, by_outcome, by_criterion, calls}`.

`totals` is `{calls, errors, seconds, prompt_tokens, cached_tokens, completion_tokens, reasoning_tokens, total_tokens, models, first_call_at, last_call_at}` — the same block the job result carries as `usage` (plus `usage_url` there). A token total is `null`, not 0, when no call reported it (`cached_tokens` needs `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` on muse-glimmer). `by_kind` (fast | escalate | score | ask | refine | verify | select | describe | other — `fast` a one-token readout, `escalate` an adaptive criterion's reasoned call on the escalation model) and `by_outcome` (ok | error) map to the same block; `by_criterion` is a LIST of blocks each with its `criterion` — `null` for the calls that belong to no criterion (the per-item selection, a reference's description).

`calls[]`, in the order made: `{id, job_id, job_type, request_id, started_at, label, kind, criterion, item, document, attempt, model_requested, model_reported, api_url, max_tokens, outcome, http_status, error, finish_reason, seconds, prompt_tokens, cached_tokens, completion_tokens, reasoning_tokens, total_tokens, usage}` — `usage` is the response's raw `usage` object; `seconds` is time inside the model's max_concurrent (models.yaml) slot (the model, not the wait); `http_status` / `error` are set on a failed request.

**200** with zero calls for a job that has not called the model (queued, or text / cv criteria only). **200 with `job_present: false`** once the TTL sweeper has removed the job — the usage rows outlive it. **404** only when there is neither a job row nor any usage row (an unknown id, or a job removed with DELETE /jobs/:jobId). See API.md § Model usage and § `GET /jobs/{job_id}/usage`. Each call carries `model_id` (the registry id) and `api_url` (the URL actually posted to); the breakdown adds `by_model`.
